name: Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons

verification.note: Group 1 controls the load unless the load is detached; then group 9 does, and group 1 only sets its LED.

steps.text: At the electrical panel, turn off the circuit breakers or remove the fuses feeding the wall box, and make sure the power is off.
Remove the wall plate from the switch, unscrew the switch and gently pull it out.
Disconnect the wires from the switch.
Turn on power.
Use a voltage meter to identify the line and load wires that were connected to the switch, and identify the neutral and ground wires.
Turn off power.
Connect the keypad's bare copper wire to ground, white to neutral, red to load and black to line. Make sure the connections are firm with no exposed wire.
With the button labels right side up, gently place the keypad into the wall box and screw it into place.
Turn on power.
steps.expect: The LED of the MAIN On/Off button and the connected light turn on

steps.text: Tap the MAIN On/Off button on and off to check that the keypad works.
steps.expect: The button LED and the load turn on and off

steps.text: Reinstall the wall plate.

notes: In 3-way and 4-way circuits every switch must be replaced by an Insteon keypad or switch. Wire one to line, neutral and load and the others to line and neutral, using one traveler to share line between boxes and capping the unused traveler and the red wire on keypads without the load. Then add them to a scene as controllers and responders of each other.

steps.text: Tap the keypad button that will control the scene.
Press and hold the SET button until the keypad beeps, about 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Beep; the scene button's LED blinks

notes: As a controller: after the keypad beeps, set the responder to the state the scene should recall and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps or its LED flashes. The keypad double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

As a responder: press and hold the controller's scene button until it beeps, tap the keypad button that should respond until its LED is in the desired state (press and hold to add the main scene at a dimmed level), then press and hold the keypad's SET button until it double-beeps. The button's LED flashes once and returns to its previous state.
For synchronized scenes, such as a 3-way circuit, link the devices as controllers and responders of each other.
If either LED keeps blinking, the addition failed; tap that device's SET button until the LED stops blinking and try again.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the keypad beeps, about 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Beep; the scene button's LED blinks

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) says i1 devices don't support Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), and the catalog doesn't know the engine of every version of this product. An i2 or i2CS version takes it; ask the device with Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) first.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Tap the scene button on the keypad.
Press and hold the SET button until the keypad beeps.
steps.expect: Scene button LED blinks; all lit LEDs brighten to 100%

steps.text: Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the desired scene state (on a keypad, tap the button at least once).
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes.
After adding all responders, tap the SET button.
steps.expect: Scene button LED stops blinking; LEDs return to normal brightness

steps.text: Tap the scene button on the keypad.
Press and hold the SET button until the keypad beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps again.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps or its LED blinks.
steps.expect: The keypad double-beeps and the scene button LED stops blinking

notes: To remove a keypad button as a responder: press and hold the controller's scene button until it beeps, press and hold it again until it beeps again, tap the keypad button to remove, then press and hold the keypad's SET button until it double-beeps.

To remove several responders at once: tap the scene button, hold the SET button until it beeps, hold it again until it beeps again, then tap it; on each responder (tap the button first on a keypad) hold the SET button until it beeps or its LED flashes; tap the keypad's SET button to finish.

steps.text: Pull the SET button out to create an air gap.
Wait 10 seconds.
Push the SET button in and hold it in.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a couple of seconds the keypad double-beeps, the LEDs return to normal brightness and the load turns on

steps.text: Remove the keypad's scene memberships from all of its responders.
Remove the keypad's scene memberships from all of its controllers.
Remove the keypad from use.

notes: Otherwise delays, error blinks and repeated retries result.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons 2486DWH8 Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Each button other than the load's can be set to toggle, send only off, or send only on.
Group 1 is button A, which controls the load. In the 6-button layout, which software can set, group 1 is the On and Off buttons and groups 3 to 6 are buttons A to D.
Group 9 controls the load only while it's detached from group 1.
sources: Dimmer Keypad, 8 Buttons 2486DWH8 Quick Start Guide
